answer: According to arXiv 2503.18979, the probability of α exceeding αc is effectively equivalent to bounding the tail probability of Y for large y. Specifically, if near αc the jump ˜x(α) scales like (α - αc)p for some p > 0, then for large y, bounding Pr(Y > y) is related to bounding Pr(α > αc). The function η(y) plays a role in this relationship by being a non-negative function that approaches zero as y approaches infinity. This means that for sufficiently large y, the bounding of Pr(Y > y) can be simplified to the bounding of Pr(α > αc), as η(y) becomes small.
